2 minutes read

Shell prompt segment

offing prompt prints a short segment for your shell prompt, such as ⏳2, when the repository you are in has lifecycle findings. It prints nothing otherwise.

offing prompt [path] [--format <text|json>] [--symbol <s>]
Flag What it does
[path] Directory to look at. Default ..
--format <text|json> text (default) prints the segment. json prints an offing.prompt.v1 document with cached, total, urgent, and count.
--symbol <s> The symbol before the count. Default ⏳. --symbol EOL: gives ASCII.

The count is the high and critical findings when there are any, otherwise all findings.

What it reads

The command reads only the scan cache for the repository root (the nearest folder with a .git). It never scans, never starts a process, and never uses the network. It always exits 0.

It prints nothing when the cache is missing or stale. The cache is stale when a file the scan read changed or disappeared after the scan, or when the scan is more than seven days old.

Refresh the cache with any of these:

  • offing scan writes it.
  • offing watch updates it on every change.
  • The pre-push hook (offing init --hooks) scans before each push, which updates it.

A cold start is kept light: offing prompt loads only its own module, not the command table or the detectors. On a warm cache it runs in under 50 ms at the 95th percentile (tests/prompt-segment.test.ts measures 50 runs).

Snippets

Each snippet runs the command only inside a git repository.

Starship

Add to ~/.config/starship.toml:

[custom.offing]
command = "offing prompt"
when = "git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree"
format = "[$output]($style) "
style = "bold yellow"

oh-my-zsh

Add to your theme file (or ~/.zshrc after source $ZSH/oh-my-zsh.sh):

offing_prompt_info() {
  git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1 || return
  local segment
  segment="$(offing prompt)"
  [[ -n "$segment" ]] && echo "%{$fg_bold[yellow]%}${segment}%{$reset_color%} "
}
PROMPT='$(offing_prompt_info)'"$PROMPT"

Powerlevel10k

In ~/.p10k.zsh, add offing to POWERLEVEL9K_RIGHT_PROMPT_ELEMENTS and define the segment:

function prompt_offing() {
  git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1 || return
  local segment
  segment="$(offing prompt)"
  [[ -n "$segment" ]] && p10k segment -f 178 -t "$segment"
}

fish

In ~/.config/fish/functions/fish_right_prompt.fish:

function fish_right_prompt
    if git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1
        set -l segment (offing prompt)
        if test -n "$segment"
            set_color yellow
            echo -n $segment
            set_color normal
        end
    end
end

bash

In ~/.bashrc:

__offing_prompt() {
  local segment=""
  if git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    segment="$(offing prompt)"
  fi
  PS1="${__offing_base_ps1}${segment:+\[\e[33m\]${segment}\[\e[0m\] }"
}
__offing_base_ps1="$PS1"
PROMPT_COMMAND="__offing_prompt${PROMPT_COMMAND:+; $PROMPT_COMMAND}"
